title: “THE ANGEL CALLED HIM MIGHTY.”
paragraphs:
Not preaching.
Not leading.
Not conquering.
Let’s step into Book of Judges 6.

Israel was crushed under Midian.
Seven years of fear.
Seven years of crops stolen.
Seven years of hiding in caves like hunted animals.
Winepresses were carved low into rock. Tight. Sunken. Defensive. You don’t thresh wheat there. You thresh on a hilltop where wind separates grain from chaff.
Because fear will shrink your calling.
Then the Angel of the Lord appears.
“The Lord is with you, mighty warrior.” (Judges 6:12)
Here’s the open wound in this story:

Gideon doesn’t feel mighty.
He feels forgotten.
“My clan is the weakest… and I am the least.” (Judges 6:15)
You ever said that in your own words?

“I’m not that gifted.”
“I’m the least in my family.”
“I messed up too much.”
“I’m just trying to survive.”
Heaven called him what he could not see in himself.

God does not deny Gideon’s fear.
He confronts it with presence.
Your weakness + His presence = courage born in secret.
Some scholars interpret the “Angel of the Lord” here as a theophany—an appearance of God Himself. Others see it as a high-ranking angelic messenger. Either way, the authority is divine.
But here’s where it gets personal.
Before Gideon fights Midian, he has to tear down his father’s altar to Baal.
God did not wait for Gideon to become fearless.
He moved while Gideon was trembling.
This is the Gospel thread running beneath the soil.

Hiding in shame.
Hiding in sin.
Hiding in our own winepress of self-protection.
At the cross, Jesus was publicly shamed so you could stop hiding privately.
At the resurrection, He proved that fear does not get the final word.
Sin does not get the final word.
Your insecurity does not get the final word.
Maybe you’re reading this from your own winepress.

Quiet.
Small.
Afraid to be seen.
And He is not mocking your fear.
But because He is with you.

Repent of unbelief.
Step out of hiding.
Trust the Savior who steps into winepresses to rescue cowards and turn them into warriors.
Jesus does not recruit the brave.
“Lord, I feel least. But if You are with me, that is enough. Tear down my idols. Build courage in me. I trust Christ alone.”
